articles.title_zh: Russian military plane crashes killing all 19 on board
facts_zh:
Russian military plane crashes killing all 19 on board
- Published
A Russian military transport plane has crashed in Siberia, killing all 19 people on board, the country's defence ministry is cited as saying by state-run media.
The An-12 aircraft went down during a "scheduled flight" in an "uninhabited area" in the Kemerovo region, the ministry said in a statement.
A technical malfunction is preliminarily believed to be the cause of Tuesday's crash, the ministry added.

articles.title_zh: UK sanctions firms over Israeli West Bank settlements

UK sanctions firms over Israeli West Bank settlements
- Published
The UK has sanctioned companies it said are involved in building settlements in the occupied West Bank, in the first package of measures since the government announced a tougher approach to Israeli actions in the territory.
The government said the sanctions against eight construction and property development firms would disrupt their flows of finance and ability to support building in the West Bank.
The construction of settlements, which are illegal under international law, has risen sharply in recent years.

articles.title_original: Trump says US taking 'very seriously' any Iranian plot against Washington
articles.title_zh: Trump says US taking 'very seriously' any Iranian plot against Washington
facts_zh:
Trump says US taking 'very seriously' any Iranian plot against Washington
- Published
President Donald Trump has said the US is taking "very seriously" the potential for any Iranian plot to attack Washington DC, after he was asked about a CNN report citing US intelligence assessments.

In the Philippines, where he attended the Asean Summit, Trump nodded when asked by a journalist about the report that Tehran was planning to detonate a so-called dirty bomb in the US capital and said: "We're looking into it."
CNN cited unnamed US intelligence officials suggesting Iran could target senior figures in Trump's administration with such an attack.
Iran called the claim "baseless." Concerns about dirty bombs grew after the 9/11 attacks in 2001, although no such attack has ever occurred.

articles.title_original: How the attack on Crimean Bridge unfolded
articles.title_zh: How the attack on Crimean Bridge unfolded
facts_zh:
How the attack on Putin's prized Crimean Bridge unfolded
- Published
Stretching across the Kerch Strait in the Black Sea, the Crimean Bridge was always a symbol: for Russia, a prestige project cementing its claim to sovereign Ukrainian territory, and for Ukraine, a hated piece of infrastructure emblematic of Moscow's occupation of the Crimean Peninsula.

A key section of the double-arched, 12-mile-long bridge now lies on the seabed, brought down by an arsenal of Ukrainian long-range weaponry in a seven-stage operation culminating in a dramatic collapse.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov has said that the bridge "will be rebuilt, and it will be even better than before".

all_titles.en: How the attack on Crimean Bridge unfolded

Police said gunmen on a motorbike ambushed Camilo Rodríguez, 50, as he was travelling in his car north of the capital, San José, on Monday afternoon.

- Published
The article has details that some readers may find disturbing
A pregnant Muslim woman who was gang-raped and saw 14 family members murdered during the 2002 Gujarat riots has spoken of her "pain, shock and disbelief" after two of her rapists were recently granted bail.
Bilkis Bano said in a statement that she heard about the top court order through press reports and vowed to fight back.
The freed men are from a group of 11 convicts - part of a Hindu mob - serving life terms for the attack on Bano.
